areas.summary: How we become who we are, and how we change.

themes.name: Boredom as a signal
themes.summary: What empty time is trying to say.

themes.name: Habits and identity
themes.summary: Small acts and the self they build.

themes.summary: Memory, meaning and the next step.

ideas.claim: Doing fewer things well leaves more room than doing many things fast.

prompts.text: What is one thing you could stop doing this week?
When did doing less give you more?

ideas.claim: Rest is part of the work, not a prize for finishing it.

prompts.text: What would change if rest did not have to be earned?
Where do you feel guilty for resting?

ideas.claim: Switching between tasks costs more attention than it seems to.

prompts.text: How many times did you switch tasks today?

ideas.claim: A full calendar can hide an empty day.

prompts.text: Which busy day last month felt empty afterwards?
What fills your time that you did not choose?

ideas.claim: Boredom is information about what you want, if you stay with it.

prompts.text: What did the last bout of boredom point at?
What do you reach for when you feel bored?

ideas.claim: Reaching for the phone hides the signal boredom sends.

prompts.text: What were you feeling the last time you picked up your phone without thinking?

ideas.claim: Every small act is a vote for who you are becoming.

prompts.text: What did you vote for today?
Which small act do you want more of?

ideas.claim: Starting badly beats waiting to start well.

prompts.text: What are you waiting to do well before you begin?

ideas.claim: Change starts with grief for the old self.

prompts.text: What did your last big change cost you?
What are you still mourning?

ideas.claim: The story about your past can change even though the past cannot.

prompts.text: Which part of your story would you tell differently now?

ideas.claim: A kinder telling of a failure makes the next try easier.

prompts.text: Retell one failure as if a friend had lived it.

ideas.claim: People want to be heard before they want advice.

prompts.text: When did someone listen to you without fixing anything?
Who in your life needs to be heard this week?

ideas.claim: A pause before answering gives the other person room to say more.

prompts.text: What happens when you wait three seconds before replying?

ideas.claim: Argue with the strongest version of an idea, not the weakest.

prompts.text: Which view do you dismiss without knowing its best case?

ideas.claim: Some arguments are about the relationship, not the topic.

prompts.text: What was your last argument really about?

ideas.claim: Productivity is mostly about the right tools.

links.why: Rest that is not earned leaves the day less crowded.

A bad start is still a vote.
A concrete way to retell the past.
The pause is how someone feels heard.
Arguing the best case assumes the topic matters; sometimes it does not.
Starting many things badly pulls against doing fewer things well.
Grieving the old self is part of retelling the story.
Tools promise speed; doing less asks for choice.

core.belief: Space comes before growth: in a day, in a mind, in a conversation.
